video_title: Giannis Is Getting His Numbers. Why Aren’t the Heat Winning?

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Doc Rivers' criticism of Giannis Antetokounmpo's playstyle and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's a really difficult guy. He has this great passing ability.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Doc Rivers is making news with the Podfather, Bill Simmons. He went on his show and the subject of Giannis and the Heat and their slow start came up. He had this to say: 'He's not easy. He plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's a really difficult guy. He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't have super IQ at the same time. He really has one way. Every play, he wants to force it. I wish he learned how to execute better. The thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shootaround to lock in on execution. Now he has a coach who's as good as there is at execution.'

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Harper
text_blocks.text: I mean, he's out of excuses. That's my add addition, not Doc Rivers.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the Milwaukee Bucks' offensive system and Giannis's role
quotes.excerpt: I don't know if Mike Budenholzer would agree with like he only plays one way.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Harper
text_blocks.text: It's not wrong, right? I think there's it might not be 100% correct. I don't know if Mike Budenholzer would agree with like he only plays one way. Budenholzer came in, put his system in, Giannis kind of played around it, won a championship, they were, you know, they were very successful in the regular season, finally broke through. I'd be curious to know if Budenholzer, I mean, Griff wasn't there long enough to have an opinion, well, Doc had something to do with that. Jason Kidd, I'd wonder if they feel the same way.

text_blocks.speaker: Wosny Lambre
text_blocks.text: Well, Doc had something to do with that.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo's role as a modern-day Shaquille O'Neal
quotes.excerpt: He is, not to overreact to it, but like a modern-day Shaquille O'Neal in that he gets 20 points.
quotes.quote: He is, not to overreact to it, but like a modern-day Shaquille O'Neal in that he gets 20 points in the paint every day, right? I mean, he lives in the paint. That's stuff that really only Shaquille O'Neal has done and Zion Williamson for like a year or two.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the Miami Heat's defensive struggles and roster issues
quotes.excerpt: People who are actually really smart at basketball are like, this team is going to be a top-five NBA defense.
quotes.quote: People who are actually really smart at basketball are like, this team is going to be a top-five NBA defense, especially when they got Bam Adebayo on the floor. They're bottom five. They've been insanely bad and I think a lot of it does have to do with their wings. Andrew Wiggins, Klay Thompson, Tim Hardaway Jr., whose minutes have been decreasing the last few games. I do think that has something to do with it, but see where I disagree with you, Zach, is I think it's all of a piece. I think Giannis puts all of his energies into getting his numbers and the defensive part of things, he's not attentive, he's not an attention-to-detail guy. He's not killing himself on defense because he's putting all of that effort into getting buckets.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on Tim Hardaway Jr.'s defensive performance
quotes.excerpt: Even when Chris Middleton was injured, like he defended better than what Tim Hardaway Jr. is doing.
quotes.quote: Even when Chris Middleton was injured, like he defended better than what Tim Hardaway Jr. is doing. Like Tim Hardaway Jr. took a charge last night and I was like, 'Oh, wow, he was in position.' That's crazy.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on the lack of post-season offensive success for Giannis
quotes.excerpt: Giannis has never been part of good post-season offense. Every year that simplistic way of attacking defenses did not work.
quotes.quote: They won that championship on defense. They were just extremely, they had an underperforming offense every single post-season. Giannis has never been part of good post-season offense. Every year that simplistic way of attacking defenses did not work. There needs to be more nuance and I think Giannis needs to embrace this.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Giannis Antetokounmpo on the struggles of the pick-and-roll with Damian Lillard
quotes.excerpt: Right now our pick-and-roll connection is people are benefiting more than us because Dame is being double-teamed.
quotes.quote: This is the craziest part. Because going into the season, you're saying like, 'Oh shit, the pick-and-roll, I'm going to get so many easy looks.' But right now our pick-and-roll connection is people are benefiting more than us because Dame is being double-teamed and when I get the ball, they're zoning up. And so it's like, swing, swing, and other people will benefit.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the defensive challenges of defending Giannis and Damian Lillard
quotes.excerpt: We got to build a fucking wall according to Stan Van Gundy. Like, now you've got two going away from you.
quotes.quote: What he's describing is what every team wants to produce. Is what any star who has been the focus of this shit for years, defenses loading up three, four guys. We got to build a fucking wall according to Stan Van Gundy. Like, now you've got two going away from you, because they're like, 'Uh oh, that guy's a killer. We can't even let him side-step from 37 feet. We've seen that. We've seen that. That's deadly. That's our defense is dead.' And so now you're essentially, you're describing you're like, 'Oh, now I got to play four-on-three basketball.' And that doesn't help. And like, yeah, one of those guys is going to come to me. So now I've got two guys open. That's not fair.

quotes.quote: Torrey Craig 43.9% from three, Gary Trent Jr. 41.6% from three, Chris Middleton 40.7%, AJ Green 42.2%. They were number one in the league in three-point percentage.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on Jimmy Butler's defensive dominance against Jrue Holiday
quotes.excerpt: Jimmy went for like 56 or whatever it was, and that whole time Jimmy like Jimmy's yelling at Drew Holiday.
quotes.quote: There was that series where Jimmy, the game Jimmy went for like 56 or whatever it was, and that whole time Jimmy like Jimmy's yelling at Drew Holiday, 'I own you.' Drew Holiday is one of the best defenders ever. Like Drew Holiday is the dude that everyone's like, 'I don't want to go against him.'

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the Milwaukee Bucks' defensive statistics
quotes.excerpt: They're 30th in three-point percentage allowed. They're getting torched. They're 29th in field goal percentage overall.
quotes.quote: They're 30th in three-point percentage allowed. They're getting torched. They're 29th in field goal percentage overall. They're 24th in two-point percentage against them. Like these are all, I mean, the thing is like they're a top eight rebounding team on defense. They're top six in not putting opponents on the line. They're 11th in forcing turnovers, but they're 30th. It's crazy if you can rebound the miss, but there's probably no one missing.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the impact of training camp on team performance
quotes.excerpt: I've talked to a bunch of players about this, former players who were back in the day when training camp was real.
quotes.quote: I've talked to a bunch of players about this, former players who were back in the day when training camp was real. When they, like Tim Legler talked about having anxiety the night before training camp started because he knew the work he was about to go through. It was three weeks to a month of two-a-days for the first couple weeks and hard practices and hard scrimmages and everything. And now they, training camp's basically a walkthrough now. So you go from, and no one plays in the preseason, you're not playing heavy minutes, so you go from, you know, just your individual workouts and stuff and some light work to, hey, here's 35 minutes on an NBA game. And the body just isn't prepared for it.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the impact of the CBA on team performance
quotes.excerpt: I think the rash of injuries is because of training camp. I think the rash of injuries, I've talked to a bunch of players.
quotes.quote: I think the rash of injuries is because of training camp. I think the rash of injuries, I've talked to a bunch of players about this, former players who were back in the day when training camp was real. I think the increase of possessions and movement adds to that that stress, but I think it starts with the lack of training camp. But this is never going to happen. Here's my issue with it, just from a standpoint of like, hey, this puts us in line with college and with the international game and everything. Who cares? This is the NBA. This is the big boy league. Like no one's like, 'Ooh, I hope I make it to, you know, to the the ACB, I hope I'm in that Spanish league, I hope I get to the Turkish league.' The nerve of you disrespecting the great hoop that they play at Real Madrid. Great professional basketball over there. It ain't us.

quotes.speaker: Zach Harper
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach Harper on the impact of the CBA and player movement
quotes.excerpt: If I told you, hey, we're going to watch a game tonight, Tyrese Haliburton, Ja Morant, Anthony Edwards.
quotes.quote: If I told you, hey, we're going to watch a game tonight, Tyrese Haliburton, Ja Morant, Anthony Edwards, Cason Wallace, Kawhi Leonard, Jalen Williams, Jaren Jackson Jr., Pala Ben Carroll, Chet Holmgren, Jalen Duren. That's our 10. We're watching those 10 guys play basketball tonight. You'd be like, 'That's going to be a great game. That's almost an All-Star game style.' Those guys are all out extended periods of time right now. Right now. First two weeks of the of the season. Like we are missing significant players at the start of every single year for an extended period of time. And so, unless like, and by the way, the Players Union wants training camp to be this way. They want it to be this light work.

quotes.quote: To Timani Kamara, I want to call him the lens cap, because he makes it real dark for all your shooters. Kamara, camera, it kind of works. All the lens cap, that's no good. We'll see how Alex Caruso does tonight. We'll see how Austin Reaves does tonight.

quotes.speaker: Wosny Lambre
quotes.summary_phrase: Wosny Lambre on Adam Silver's 40-minute NBA game proposal
quotes.excerpt: Your guy, my guy, our guy, the great Adam Silver, commissioner of the NBA, has floated the idea.
quotes.quote: Your guy, my guy, our guy, the great Adam Silver, commissioner of the NBA, has floated the idea of a 40-minute NBA game. I've seen a lot of people receive this with derision. I'm not on the derisive side, honestly. I don't think this is the worst idea ever. I think it does make the NBA more uniform with the rest of the entire basketball world, when you talk about college, when you talk about international. I don't think this is a bad idea, especially with the possessions inflation that we now have in the modern NBA, where there's just so many more possessions than there used to be. I just don't think this is what actually stops the rash of injuries.
